pairs.difference: A: the cap board and band are quiet satin cloth with soft edges and almost no surface marks, like the restrained real finish. B: the boot shaft carries an even speckled leather noise, and the overlay shapes have sharp raised edges. The foot is lacquered smoothly, so grain and gloss split abruptly at the strap.
pairs.fix: Draw the boot as soft, smooth leather with a low satin sheen. Remove the speckled grain from the shaft and keep the overlay edges soft and quiet.

pairs.difference: A: the rope has twisted strands with fine, matte fibre streaks, which reads as rope, though the numbers sit at the top of the real range. B: the neckerchief has no weave or cloth softness. Its folds are swollen rubber with one even sheen, and the emblem is hard enamel. Weak call, because real cards are also smooth.
pairs.fix: Make the neckerchief soft matte cotton: thin folded edges, gentle creases, no rubbery sheen, with a slightly satin metal badge.

pairs.difference: A: the jacket has soft matte twill, quiet seams and glossy enamel badges, a believable matte and shiny mix, though its detail sits just above the real ceiling. B: the hat is smooth waxy felt with soft shading and a satin star. Neither surface breaks the real finish clearly.

A: the anchor is smooth satin blue painted metal with soft edge highlights, and the rope twist is fine and quiet. B: the caravan has soft cream matte panels, satin trim and a modest wheel-hub shine, close to the real computer finish. Both stay in range with no telling marks.

A: the mug has drawn brushed-metal streaks, a credible metal with quiet table grain, though its detail falls below the real range. B: the arch packs crisp petals and hundreds of leaves, each with its own hard glossy shine, and the gloss, detail and micro texture all overshoot the real ceiling. The whole object is equally lacquered.
pairs.fix: Use fewer, larger, soft-edged leaves with a matte surface. Keep shine to a few small highlights on the roses, and soften the petal edges and the small marks.

pairs.difference: A: the computer is the same real card shown in the lessons, with soft matte plastic and almost no surface marks. B: the saddle has dashed pale contrast stitching on every edge, pebbled leather grain, crisp rivets and a punched strap. That is the same small, busy finish seen on the generated gloves.
pairs.fix: Make the saddle smooth, soft leather with a gentle sheen. Remove the dashed stitching and pebbled grain, and use only a few simple soft seams and one plain buckle.

pairs.difference: A: the doors have soft satin wood with fine, fairly quiet grain in the lower panels, close to the real podium. B: the shoes have a crisp regular dot mesh, candy-glossy laces and a rubbery sole, all equally shiny. The gloss share sits at the top of the real range, and the upper reads as moulded plastic, not textile.
pairs.fix: Make the upper soft matte fabric with a barely visible mesh, the laces matte cord, and the sole a dull rubber with one soft highlight.

pairs.difference: A: the cart mixes materials well, with clear glass streaks, matte popcorn, satin gold posts and flat red paint. B: the cactus is one waxy green plastic, and its spines are enlarged capsule shapes, like chunky toy details. It has no skin variation or matte areas.
pairs.fix: Give the cactus a matte, slightly dry skin with subtle tone variation, and replace the capsule spines with tiny thin pale needles.

pairs.difference: A: the barrel staves carry big looping grain lines, the iron bands have scratch marks, and an orange stain sits on one stave, so the texture is large and decorative. B: the chest has quiet plank lines, satin gold and smooth coins with restrained marks, closer to the real finish.
pairs.fix: Keep the wood smooth with only faint, fine straight grain. Remove the large grain loops, scratches and orange stain, and make the iron bands plain satin metal.

pairs.difference: A: the wagon cover is matte canvas with soft folds over satin wood and small brass studs, a clear gloss mix. B: the boat is more uniformly varnished orange wood with soft plank lines and fine rope twist. The boat is slightly more lacquered, but both stay in range and match the real restraint.

A: the locomotive has crisp rivets, many small pipe and bolt details and sharp rim light across dark metal, and its gloss share exceeds the real ceiling. B: the coaster has soft smooth painted plastic with few marks and broad gentle highlights, like the real slide. The train is the busier, sharper surface.
pairs.fix: Reduce the rivets and small parts, make the boiler a soft satin dark metal with one broad highlight, and soften the edge shine.

pairs.difference: A: the gloves are blurred, inflated red balloons with no leather feel or seams, only a few pinched creases, and the shine is a soft glow. Detail, micro texture and gloss all fall below the real floor. B: the snorkel has believable translucent silicone with a clear lens reflection and defined rim edges, so its material reads correctly.
pairs.fix: Draw the gloves as firm, soft leather with a satin sheen, one or two clean seams, a defined cuff and crisp small highlights, in sharper focus.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away through surfaces that are either overworked or swollen. Overworked ones have dashed stitching, pebbled grain, big looping wood grain, scratches, and crisp small repeated parts such as rivets, mesh or leaves, each with its own hard shine. Swollen ones are uniform rubber or wax with no material difference, plus capsule-like toy details. Real cards are softer and quieter, with few marks, gentle broad highlights and a clear matte-to-satin mix within one object.
